The declared 200 schema's `defects[]` items are full issue-link records: id, issue_id, issue_type, issue_status, priority, record_status, entity_type, entity_id, entity_uuid, project_id, metadata (free-form object), created_at, updated_at -- not the slim {issue_id, issue_type} shape. Worth noting for contrast: the *embedded* `issues[]` array returned inline on each row of the sibling list_exploratory_sessions IS the slim {issue_id, issue_type} shape (required: issue_id, issue_type only) -- so the two 'issues/defects' shapes in this API are genuinely different sizes depending on which endpoint you read them from, and this capability's contract is honest about which one it is.
2. Session-vs-log coverage: CONFIRMED. The schema carries entity_type (values illustrated: 'ExploratorySession' vs 'ExploratorySessionLog') and entity_id, and guidance is explicit: 'This is the session-wide view: rows carry entity_type and entity_id, so the list can include both links made on the session itself and links made on individual log entries. That is also the extent of the documented overlap statement -- it says a log's own `defects` field is the log-scoped subset of what this session-wide endpoint returns, but does not spell out whether the log-level `defects` field embeds the exact same record shape (id/issue_status/priority/etc.) or the slimmer {issue_id, issue_type} shape; that would need the sibling probing list_exploratory_session_logs to confirm from its side, per the prompt's own note that it's asked the same question.

Guidance states directly: 'Paging uses `p`, NOT `page`.', '`per_page` is accepted and ignored -- the page size is fixed at 30. Walk `p` until a page comes back short.', and 'There are no filters on this endpoint: no status, tracker or date narrowing. Filter client-side.' No other query params are declared at all.
